description: Nine two-input arithmetic cells — three dividing, three raising to a power and three multiplying — and six single-input logarithms

inputs.text: The A side of one A*B cell, which sets how many channels that cell's output carries
The A side of one A/B cell, which sets how many channels that cell's output carries
The A side of one A to the power B cell, which sets how many channels that cell's output carries
The B side of one A*B cell, read channel by channel against the A side
The B side of one A/B cell, the divisor, read channel by channel against the A side
The B side of one A to the power B cell, the exponent, read channel by channel against the A side
The input to one natural logarithm
The input to one base 2 logarithm
The input to one base 10 logarithm

outputs.text: A times B for that cell, in volts, with no scaling and no limit
A divided by B for that cell, in volts, with no scaling and no limit
A raised to the power B for that cell, in volts, with no scaling and no limit
The natural logarithm of the voltage at its own In jack
The base 2 logarithm of the voltage at its own In jack
The base 10 logarithm of the voltage at its own In jack

notes: A cell is worked out only while both of its inputs and its own output are patched; with any of the three missing the output jack holds whatever value it last had.
Each cell takes its channel count from its A input, and reads the B input channel by channel, so a one-channel B against a polyphonic A gives 0V on every channel past the first.
Nothing here is scaled or clipped. Dividing by 0V, or taking the logarithm of 0V or of a negative voltage, puts an infinity or a not-a-number on the output jack and into whatever it feeds.
